chunks: His father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them) narrated, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isbahani, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

There is no good in the world except for one of two men: a man who increases in goodness every day, and a man who compensates for his sin through repentance. But where will he find repentance? And by God, if he prostrated until his neck broke, God would not accept from him except through our Wilayah, the Ahl al-Bayt.
ai.seo_question: What are the two types of people who possess goodness in this world according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the two paths to worldly goodness as continuous spiritual growth and sincere repentance, but he elevates these acts by anchoring their acceptance in the Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt. This reflects the Shia theological principle that external worship (*ibadat*) is validated and perfected by internal allegiance (*wilayah*), ensuring that even the most extensive physical devotion, such as prolonged prostration, is accepted by God only when coupled with this divine authority.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-29 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father and Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullahquoted on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isbahany, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Davood al-Minqari, on the authority of Hafs ibn Qiyath al-Nakha’ee that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“There is no good in this world except for two men: a man who does more good deeds every day, and a man who compensates for his sins through repentance. When will he be able to repent? I swear by God that God would not accept his repentance even if he prostrates to God to the extent that his neck falls off, unless by his friendship with us - the members of the Holy Household.”
